question: If secA = (13)/(5)and A is acute, find sinA
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the standard **Pythagorean Triple (5, 12, 13)**.

Since **sec A = 13/5**, we have **Hypotenuse (H) = 13** and **Base (B) = 5**.

The **Perpendicular (P)** corresponds to the third side of the triple, which is **12**.

The value of **sin A = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = 12/13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12/13.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec A = 13/5 and **A** is an **acute angle**.

**Formula Used:** sin A = √(1 − cos²A) or P² + B² = H²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87698fe6e90ff7fcb35d8c6e6738cb09545cebface49d18e7717ab621b8c1e51.png] 

⇒ cos A = 1 / sec A = 5/13

⇒ sin A = √(1 − cos²A)

⇒ sin A = √(1 − (5/13)²)

⇒ sin A = √(1 − 25/169) = √(144/169)

⇒ sin A = 12/13

**∴ The correct answer is 12/13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental relation is **sin²A + cos²A = 1**, which holds for any angle A.

Pythagorean Triples

Common right-angled triangle side ratios (triples) include **(3, 4, 5)**, **(5, 12, 13)**, **(8, 15, 17)**, and **(7, 24, 25)**.

Acute Angle Ratios

For an **acute angle A** (0° < A < 90°), all trigonometric ratios like **sin A**, **cos A**, and **tan A** are positive.</p
